data.name: Ren of Wake Island I: The Genin Beneath the Tide
data.description: Ren, an impressionable Genin candidate, joins you to investigate missing ships, lantern smugglers, and the sea cave beneath Wake Island.
data.successDescription: Ren remains in the Tidebreaker Program, changed by the first lesson you gave them.

objectives.description: A Tidebreaker instructor assigns Ren to you at the Bureau. Ren bows too quickly and watches how you answer.
Travel with Ren to the Eastern Docks and inspect the missing cargo manifests.
The dockworker's hands shake. He knows more than he admits. Ren waits to see what kind of pressure you use.
Ren whispers, 'You did not even raise your voice, and he still talked. I did not know strength could look like that.'
Ren's eyes harden. 'He gave us what we needed. Maybe being feared is better than being respected.'
Ren nods from the rain shadow. 'Observation can cut deeper than threats.'
Ren stumbles at first, then steadies. 'You trusted me with the silence between answers. I will remember that.'
Follow the lantern marks to a warehouse where stolen supplies move under debt contracts.
Inside the warehouse, smugglers hide behind poor workers forced into crime. Ren studies where you place blame.

nextObjectiveId.text: Burn the warehouse as a warning.

objectives.description: Ren lowers their voice. 'Law first. Sympathy after. That is clean, even when it hurts.'
Ren looks relieved. 'Victims and predators can stand in the same room. Justice should know the difference.'
Ren watches the workers bargain for safety. 'Desperate people can become assets if someone gives them a price.'
Ren stares into the smoke. 'A message people fear is still a message they obey.'
Break the smuggler guard line before the warehouse alarm reaches the reef caves.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The warehouse fight collapses. Regroup with Ren at the lantern trail.
Descend through the tide tunnel toward the sea cave beneath the Red Reef.
Ren freezes when the cave ambusher lunges. Decide under pressure and survive the first true battle.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The Red Reef fight goes wrong. Pull Ren back to the tide tunnel and try again.
After the ambush, Ren cannot meet your eyes. The moment will become their first real lesson.
Ren clutches their sleeve. 'You moved before I could deserve it. Does that mean a teammate has value before they are useful?'
Ren swallows hard. 'No one can breathe for me. I understand.'
Ren's face goes still. 'So fear can be placed like a trap. Even mine.'
Ren bows until their hair hides their eyes. 'I will not freeze again. I will not be the weak point.'
Return to the Tidebreaker Bureau and report what the Red Reef concealed.
Command asks if Ren should remain in the Tidebreaker Program. Ren stands close enough to hear.

nextObjectiveId.text: Lie and say Ren was perfect.

objectives.description: Ren blinks through the rain. 'You did not hide what went wrong, but you did not throw me away either.'
Ren nods once. 'If shame makes me sharper, I will learn to carry it.'
Ren's smile is small and uncertain. 'A report can become armor, even when it is not true.'
Ren takes a breath. 'I was afraid. I acted late. I want another mission anyway.'
Outside, Ren asks what matters more: not feeling fear, or acting anyway?
Ren repeats the words like a hand seal. 'Acting anyway. Then courage is something you do, not something you wait to feel.'
Ren's expression closes. 'Then I will become someone fear cannot find.'
Ren looks back toward the reef. 'A frightened person sees details others miss. I can use that.'
Ren nods slowly. 'A leader carries the consequence after the fear has passed.'
Ren survives their first Tidebreaker mission and begins shaping a worldview from your example.

data.name: Ren of Wake Island II: The Black Water Trial
data.description: Ren investigates forbidden chakra stimulants, institutional rot, and the cost of truth in Wake Island's Tidebreaker Program.
data.successDescription: Ren receives recognition, but the mask display leaves a sharper question behind.

objectives.description: Ren returns steadier, promoted in expectation if not yet in certainty. The Lower District reports forbidden chakra stimulants.
Go to the Lower District infirmary and question the Genin who bought strength.
The hospitalized Genin admits he bought the drug because he was falling behind clan-born students.
Ren watches the boy breathe easier. 'Weakness is not always failure. Sometimes it is a wound.'
Ren's jaw tightens. 'If wanting power ruins you, maybe ruin is the price of being weak.'
Ren nods. 'Mercy can be a negotiation. He lives, and the truth moves.'
Ren looks at the chart beside the bed. 'Shame opens mouths faster than kindness.'
Follow the names to the illegal clinic where black water stimulants are refined.
Subdue the clinic sentinel before the rogue medical-nin destroys the patient ledger.

objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.

objectives.description: The clinic locks down. Regroup outside the black water drain and enter again.
The rogue medical-nin claims Wake Island created the demand by favoring the gifted and abandoning the rest.

nextObjectiveId.text: Spare the medic if they treat victims.
Take the research for Wake Island.

objectives.description: Ren looks over the broken vials. 'A dangerous system should not be managed. It should end.'
Ren studies the medic's shaking hands. 'Redemption can have conditions.'
Ren closes the ledger. 'Power should not be wasted just because dirty hands found it first.'
Ren's voice drops. 'Controlled corruption is still control.'
Bring the ledger to the Tidebreaker Candidate Yard, where a rival waits in the rain.
The rival candidate accuses Ren of being protected. End the challenge before it becomes a riot.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The candidate yard turns against you. Pull Ren out and face the rival again.
The rival says Ren only advances because you protect them. Ren looks shaken for the first time in months.

nextObjectiveId.text: Recruit the rival as an informant.

objectives.description: Ren's eyes soften. 'You did not have to stand between me and their words. You did anyway.'
Ren steps forward. 'My strength has to be mine when you are not there.'
Ren watches the crowd turn. 'Dominance protects reputation faster than truth.'
Ren tilts their head. 'An enemy can become a tool before they become a friend.'
Present the stimulant ledger to Wake Island command under black rain.
The ledger proves instructors ignored the stimulant trade because it produced stronger candidates.
Ren looks toward the gathered candidates. 'Truth can break a hall and still be worth speaking.'
Ren folds the ledger. 'Justice can be selective if the village survives.'
Ren's promotion badge feels heavy. 'Institutions are people too, just harder to mourn.'
Ren reads the names aloud, then chooses what Wake Island is allowed to know. Their voice does not shake.
After the hearing, Ren stares at the Global ANBU mask display and asks if truth can become an enemy.
Ren touches the glass. 'Then a village that cannot survive truth was already bleeding.'
Ren nods slowly. 'A blade in the open causes panic. A blade in the dark ends the threat.'
Ren turns away from the mask. 'Then the program exists for candidates, not the other way around.'
Ren's reflection overlaps the mask. 'Peace may need someone willing to be misunderstood.'
Ren earns Chunin recognition beneath black rain, and begins applying your values without asking.

data.name: Ren of Wake Island III: The Mask Beyond Borders
data.description: Ren enters the border crisis as a Jonin and Global ANBU candidate, carrying the lessons you gave them into a war that may begin with one wrong truth.
data.successDescription: Ren chooses the face beneath the Tidebreaker Mask and steps into their future.

objectives.description: Ren is no longer nervous. They are calm, capable, and starting to act before asking. Wake Island assigns you to stop a border war.
Travel to the neutral sandbar where both allied villages claim the other side drew first blood.
Survivors are wounded, angry, and lying. Ren waits for the method you choose when war is one bad answer away.

nextObjectiveId.text: Plant false evidence to delay retaliation.

objectives.description: Ren kneels beside the tracks. 'Patience can prevent war before anyone praises it.'
Ren listens to a survivor break. 'Pressure creates answers. Whether they are true is the next problem.'
Ren pockets the forged marker. 'A lie can buy time for the truth to arrive.'
Ren does not look away from the bodies. 'Sacrifice can reveal truth. That does not make it clean.'
Move to the prisoner skiff where a flagless provocateur waits under guard.
The prisoner's escorts attack to erase the interrogation. Keep the provocateur alive long enough to speak.

objectives.description: The skiff fight breaks formation. Return to the prisoner route and secure the witness.
The provocateur tells Ren that peace is just violence wearing clean clothes.

nextObjectiveId.text: Refuse torture and seek another way.

objectives.description: Ren's hands unclench. 'Restraint under pressure is not weakness. It is command.'
Ren asks three quiet questions. The prisoner answers the fourth before it is spoken.
Ren watches without flinching. 'Cruelty can be acceptable if the alternative is worse. That is what you showed me.'
Ren studies the prisoner's fear. 'Enemies can be resources with a pulse.'
Return to Wake Island Summit Hall before the ambassadors arrive armed.
The summit begins with incomplete truth. Assassins prepare to kill both ambassadors and leave the war no witness.

nextObjectiveId.text: Reveal truth and trust the ambassadors.
Control the summit from the shadows.

objectives.description: Ren looks almost young again. 'Trust is risky, but maybe peace cannot breathe without it.'
Ren's voice is calm. 'Peace can be engineered if no one sees the hands.'
Ren wipes their blade. 'Dead enemies cannot complicate the story.'
Ren steps ahead of you. 'I already know what you would do. Now I need to know what I will do.'
Hold the summit floor against the assassins before the ambassadors turn on each other.

objectives.description: The summit fractures. Return to the hall approach and stop the assassination cleanly.
Follow Ren to the chamber where the Tidebreaker Mask waits.
The enemy leader offers Ren a place beyond Wake Island. Ren turns to you for the final face beneath the mask.

nextObjectiveId.text: Gray Tide: peace works in shadow.

objectives.description: Ren becomes the White Tide. 'A shinobi's hands will never stay clean. That does not mean their heart has to rot.'
Ren becomes the Black Tide. 'You taught me results matter more than excuses. I stopped pretending there were lines.'
Ren becomes the Gray Tide. 'Heroes save people where others can see. Shinobi save them where no one asks the cost.'
Ren becomes the Redeemed Blade. 'Someone should have told me power was not purpose. So I will tell them.'
Ren's Tidebreaker candidacy ends with a mask, a path, and the shape of every lesson you let them keep.

objectives.description: To take the Genin Exam, you must travel to Wake Island and find the location where the exam will take place.
Welcome to Wake Island. There are many buildings here, so let’s take a quick tour of them.
The Administration Building is where you go to collect events. The Anbu HQ is where you pick up story quests.

In the Souvenir Building, you can purchase exclusive event items. The Colosseum allows you to spectate fights happening all around you. At the Science Building, you can do what we call a bloodline check.
Yes, even though you currently have a pre-selected bloodline, recent advances in genetic engineering allow you to acquire more advanced and powerful bloodlines as you become stronger.
Feel free to look around Wake Island and inspect the different buildings and options. You are strong enough for the Genin rank, so the next step is to choose which main village to join.
TNR has 5 great shinobi villages: Akikaze, Shirohana, Akasumi, Tsukimori, and Hyorin. Each village has a deity that they worship, a corresponding element, and a village bloodline.
Let’s talk about Akikaze, the Hidden Wind Village. At Akikaze, they praise Fujin, the Wind God, and their village bloodline is the dust element bloodline Aerathiel.
Next up is the Sun Village, Shirohana, located in the desert. Shirohana’s deity is Amaterasu, and their village bloodline is called Taiyo Kami of the Scorch element.
Akasumi is the Hidden Storm Village. Their deity is Watatsumi, and their village bloodline is Arashima of the Storm element.
We now have Tsukimori, the Moon Forest Village. Their deity is Tsukiyomi, and their village bloodline is Shinseina Ki of the Wood element.
Last but not least, Hyorin, the Hidden Ice Village. Located in the coldest parts of the land, their deity is Okami, and their village bloodline is the Ice element Hyouga Yui.

data.name: Shadows in the Updraft: The Lost Current
data.description: A Genin side story in Akikaze Village. A routine wind-gauge inspection uncovers the Lost Current, a missing Sky Maiden, and treason inside the Sky Wardens.
data.successDescription: You survive Kael's vacuum burst and carry Yumi's evidence out of the tunnels. The Divine Fragment is gone, but the conspiracy is exposed.

objectives.description: The copper vanes of the Lower Spires whir with their usual drone, but your brass anemometer shows the primary updraft from the Third Vent dropping fast.
Senior Warden Kael drops from a guide-rail above you. He jokes at first, then sees the readings and goes still.
You warn that a thirty percent drop could destabilize the commercial platforms below the Spire of Whispers by dusk.
Kael calls it the Lost Current and tells you to file the report with Civil Harmony. His tone makes the order feel like a wall.
Bypass Civil Harmony and climb toward the Spire of Whispers to look for someone willing to speak plainly.
Near the launch platforms, Yumi struggles to reel in a massive oracle kite. Its chakra-conductive script is scorched and torn to ribbons.
You identify the damage as vacuum-blade scoring, not heat. Yumi realizes you are paying attention to the right details.
Yumi says someone is rerouting the core wind channels with high-altitude Aero-Vault technology.
The Sky Maiden investigated the auxiliary vents last night and never returned. Yumi says the silence around her disappearance is deliberate.
Yumi names the Rogue Wardens, a splinter faction inside Kael's division, as the ones who caused the power drop.
Tomorrow's Zephyr Kage ascension will happen with Akikaze's barrier network weakened. An assassin could cross the sky-bridges unseen.
Navigate the Dust Maelstrom tunnels beneath the village, following fine sand patterns disturbed by unnatural vacuum pressure.
The trail leads to a hidden auxiliary terminal tied directly to the main power station.
Kael stands before a pressurized Aero-Vault, extracting an incandescent blue Divine Fragment used to stabilize the regional atmosphere.
Kael says the Council worships flow while Akikaze stagnates. He claims the new Zephyr Kage will disarm the village into weakness.
Kael admits the Sky Maiden is bound in the upper sanctuary. He insists she will be released once the transition of power fails.
Yumi bursts from an overhead ventilation duct and disrupts Kael's vacuum field with chakra-infused oracle daggers.
Yumi exposes the deeper betrayal: Kael is selling Akikaze's defensive layout to an underground faction from Shroud.
Kael says you are both too late. The currents have already shifted. He unleashes a localized vacuum that steals the air from your lungs.
You survive long enough to carry Yumi's evidence out of the tunnels. Kael has escaped with the Divine Fragment, but the Lost Current conspiracy is no longer hidden.

data.name: Strange Tastes
data.description: Something’s gone wrong with a new “culinary innovation” commissioned by McRamen. The laboratories insist it’s nothing dangerous… just a small experimental mishap. Still, shinobi are asked for assistance before word spreads and the problem gets out of hand. Track down the runaway creation and secure it before anyone else gets hurt
data.successDescription: You have successfully captured the rogue Triceranuggy. Dr. Kim’s research can now continue, and the village can rest a little easier. But whispers remain—if one nugget could roam free, others surely lurk in the shadows. This victory is only the first bite in a much larger feast of chaos.

objectives.description: At the mission hall, you find the familiar figure of the quest giver, a woman whose presence feels like both command and shadow. Her eyes linger on you with sharp amusement, as though she already knows you’ll accept before you even open your mouth.

So, you’ve come. Good. I have a task… unusual, but necessary. McRamen’s latest scheme to ‘improve flavor’ has gone awry. Their tinkering birthed… things that were never meant to walk this world. You are needed in Dr. Kim’s lab. Go, and hear the details from them. Consider this your first taste of the chaos they’ve stirred.

You set out through the village streets, where the golden arches of McRamen loom from every ramen stall like watchful eyes. Whispers follow you—rumors of strange sightings near the outskirts, animals that were never animals at all. The air smells faintly of fried batter and ozone. You have to reach the Lab before things escalate further.

Thank the gods you’re here! I… may have made a small miscalculation. McRamen wanted a compound to ‘enhance authenticity.’ Dr. Kim made the initial formula but… I tried to improve it and well… when applied to their test batch of chicken nuggets…

…well, they became authentic in ways no one intended. Living, breathing… prehistoric. I require your help. One of them, a triceratops-like specimen, was spotted nearby. I will give you the coordinates. Please subdue it and send it here. My research depends on it.
One more thing… I think my formula made these nuggets absorb any chakra they find in nature… We’re not sure yet how far they’ve taken these abilities.

Not far from the lab, you come upon torn-up earth and deep impressions pressed into the mud. The tracks are oddly familiar—like an elephant or rhinoceros—but broader, heavier, and scattered with crumbs of breading.

You follow the trail through thinning woods until the sound of chewing reaches your ears. Ahead, a squat creature with a breaded hide and tiny, glistening eyes gnaws on a patch of grass. Steam wafts from its body as though it had just left the fryer. The Triceranuggy raises its head, noticing you.
The creature gobbles down the offering, then suddenly glows. Its body hardens, its horns sharpen, and the triceratops nugget roars, twice its previous strength.
The nugget charges at you, stubborn but manageable in its current form.

data.name: The Archive Remembers
data.description: A distortion in the chakra fields erased techniques from living memory. The Grand Archive keeps backups of the forgotten.
data.successDescription: The forgotten techniques are restored from the Archive's backups.

objectives.description: The Archivist looks up from a lectern of drifting glyphs. "You felt it too. A sudden distortion tore through the chakra fields last night, and techniques were ripped out of living memory. Names, forms, whole schools of practice, gone as if never written."

"Fortunately, forgetting is a thing the Archive refuses to do. Every technique ever practiced in Seichi leaves an imprint here. We keep backups of the forgotten, sealed in ink and patience. Hold still, this will take several unsealings."

The Archivist slides two lacquered cases across the lectern. "First, the event seals. The Cleave and the Hollow Veil were bound to scrolls, so the scrolls come back first. Break them open when you are ready."

The Archivist unseals a shelf of tide and current techniques. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Abyssal Surge, Amaterasu's Renewal, Aqua Dragon Barrage, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a rack of flame and ember forms. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Crimson Spires, Crimson Tides, Debilitating Sword Strike, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a drawer of stone and earthwork methods. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Echoing Rift, Eclipse Drain, Endless Drowning, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a case of storm and lightning practice. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Fireball, Gale Force Blast, Infernal Ascension, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a folio of wind and gale arts. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Lightning Flash Strike, Majestic Flame, Mizukumi, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a binding of shadow and eclipse work. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Purifying Wave, Shrapnel Clone Barrage, Stone Pillar Strike, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a tray of temple and spirit forms. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Tempest of Shadows, Thunder Chain Slash, Thunder’s Judgement, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a final ledger of stray and singular techniques. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Tides of Sovereignty, Tornado Vortex, Volt Fang, and their kin. Restored, as they were."
"That is the last of them. The distortion has passed, and the field holds. If anything else has slipped your mind, come back. The Archive remembers, even when Seichi forgets."
The Archive falls quiet as the last seal settles.

data.name: The Ascension Ceremony
data.description: A new clan leader, Lady Suzume Aerathiel, has been chosen to ascend during Akikaze's sacred leadership ceremony. Before the rites can begin, an assassin infiltrates the preparations, kidnaps Suzume, and announces plans to execute her before the ceremony bell rings. Investigate the attack, track the assassin through Akikaze's ceremonial routes, and rescue the chosen leader before her ascension becomes a public tragedy.
data.successDescription: You have rescued Lady Suzume Aerathiel, defeated the assassin sent to execute her, and preserved the Ascension Ceremony. Akikaze's people witness their new clan leader rise not through unchallenged peace, but through survival, courage, and the unbroken flow of the wind.

objectives.description: Saeji of the Sky Wardens: “Lady Suzume Aerathiel is to ascend today as her clan's new leader. The pavilion is full, the banners are up, and every important person in Akikaze is pretending not to watch everyone else for weakness. In other words, a perfect day for someone to attempt something stupid, expensive, and treasonous.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Clan politics are not my concern.

objectives.description: Zephyr Kage Maemi: “This ceremony is more than tradition. The Aerathiel clan anchors much of Akikaze's wind mastery and military prestige. If Suzume is harmed before her ascension, the clan may fracture, and our enemies will smell weakness in the air.”
Inspect the Aerathiel Preparation Hall before Lady Suzume begins the procession.
objectives.successDescription: The hall is elegant and quiet. Lady Suzume stands before an ancestral mirror while attendants prepare her ceremonial mantle.

objectives.description: Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “So you are the one Saeji trusts when the wind turns sharp. Good. I would rather have honest eyes near me today than flattering mouths. Too many people celebrate an ascension while quietly measuring where the new leader may bleed.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Who would want to stop your ascension?
You seem calm for someone in danger.

objectives.description: Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “Expect? No. Prepare for? Always. The Aerathiel name carries honor, influence, and old resentments. Some prefer a leader they can control. I am not built for leashwork.”

Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “Rivals within the clan, enemies outside it, old families who dislike change, and perhaps someone offended by the tragic scandal of a woman with a spine. The list is long. The patience is short.”
Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “Fear wastes breath. I may need mine later.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Let's make sure you keep it.

objectives.description: Escort Lady Suzume from the preparation hall toward the Wind-Chime Processional Path.
objectives.successDescription: The first chimes ring in proper sequence, but the third chime cracks instead of sounding. A smoke charm bursts among the attendants.

objectives.description: Masked infiltrators disguised as ceremonial attendants attack the procession, attempting to separate Suzume from her guards.

objectives.failDescription: The assassins overwhelm you, and the ceremony deadline slips away.
objectives.fleeDescription: You abandon the pursuit, leaving Lady Suzume to the assassin.
objectives.successDescription: The smoke clears, but Lady Suzume is gone. Her silver hairpin lies on the stone, stained with pressure poison.

objectives.description: Saeji of the Sky Wardens: “They did not come to kill her here. They came to take her. The third chime was altered to mask a displacement gust. Someone planned this with temple timing and security knowledge.”
Elder Shion: “The procession chimes were not merely broken. They were made to ring out of sequence. To the crowd, it will look like the ceremony rejected her. That is the true wound they seek.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Announce the kidnapping to the crowd.

data.name: The Ashen Lung
data.description: The mining settlement of Ironvein is choking. Miners from the newly opened eastern shaft have come up coughing black dust, grey-lipped, their chests rattling, unable to draw a full breath. As a medical specialist you must diagnose the affliction, deduce and gather the components for a drawing poultice, and treat the miners before the shaft claims them.
data.successDescription: The poultice draws the black dust from the miners' lungs. Their breathing eases, the grey fades from their lips, and Ironvein breathes again, the eastern shaft sealed until it can be made safe. Your sharp medical mind saved the settlement.

objectives.description: A soot-streaked foreman meets you at the gate, his voice a dry rasp. "Thank the spirits, a healer. My miners came up from the new eastern shaft coughing black dust, and now they can't draw a full breath. Grey lips, rattling chests. None of our healers has seen its like. Please, find what's stealing the air from their lungs."

You examine a stricken miner. His lips are ashen grey, his breath a shallow wet rattle, and when he coughs a fine black residue stains his hand. No fever, no swelling, nothing fights back. This is not a sickness running its course; it is a system being slowly smothered. What is your initial diagnosis?
"Something they breathed, not something they caught." Tetsu nods grimly. "That fits, and it was the diggers on the new eastern shaft who dropped first, before anyone else took ill. Where do we look?"
You descend into the new eastern shaft, lantern guttering in the close, dust-thick air.
Deep at the shaft face you find the source: a dark seam weeping a fine black dust into every breath of air. You seal a sample in a vial for analysis.
The dust is no living pathogen. It is a fine mineral grit, coating the lungs and smothering them from within. Force will not cough it loose. What is the correct medical approach?

nextObjectiveId.text: Draw It Out With a Poultice

objectives.description: You leave the shaft to seek a drawing agent, a deposit of fine medicinal clay along the old riverbank.
Along the cutbank you find a vein of pale, cool clay, the kind that pulls poison from a wound. You gather a portion.
The clay will draw the grit, but the miners' airways are raw and clenched tight. You need a third agent to soothe the lining and open the breath. What do you add to the poultice?
You work the cool clay, the cooling mint, and the bound black dust into a thick grey salve. The Ashvein Poultice is ready. It will draw the mineral from the lungs and ease the airways open.
You carry the finished poultice back up the shaft and through the gates of Ironvein.

You pack the poultice across the miners' chests and steep it in steam. Within the hour the black rattle softens, grey lips flush back to pink, and the first full breath in days rises around you. Tetsu grips your arm, eyes wet. "You gave them back the air. Ironvein won't forget it."

data.name: The Concord Table
data.description: Forty years of war end tonight at one table in Kilnreach, and every house seated there has already paid for your services. Three doors in. Five favors out. The door you take decides everything after it.
data.successDescription: One favor stood, one signet earned, and the Concord survives its first night. The table seats five houses and one empty chair, and somewhere in Kilnreach a dead fire is warm.

objectives.description: The letter finds you at dusk, unsigned, unhurried. One seal in five colors, pressed once. Forty years of war end tonight at a table in Kilnreach, and every house seated there has already paid for your services. The Concord Table convenes at moonrise. Come as you are, or as someone useful.

Kilnreach's Concord hall has three ways in, and the way you enter is the person you are all night. The front gate takes guests. The service terraces take staff. The kiln tunnels below take no names at all.

nextObjectiveId.text: The front gate, as a guest

objectives.description: The front gate swallows you into lamplight and perfume. Guests are courted here, watched here, and priced here, usually in that order.
Three conversations glitter within reach of the wine. Which do you drift toward?

nextObjectiveId.text: The widow with the red thread

objectives.description: Two Brassmark cousins argue over whether peace is cheaper than war. They conclude, with some sorrow, that it is.
An old woman winds red thread through her fingers and watches everyone who watches her. She smiles at you a beat too early.
Orchard people speak softly about harvests and softer about funerals. Nobody in the circle drinks first.
A wall of ceremony steps into your path: the Kilnreach Doorwarden, who decides who is a guest and who is merely inside. Your invitation, it seems, requires a demonstration.
The Doorwarden rolls one shoulder. The demonstration begins.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: You are helped politely off the floor. The gate does not apologize; it simply waits for a better demonstration.
The Doorwarden bows a fraction of an inch, which in this hall is a standing ovation. Doors that were pretending to be walls quietly resume being doors.
You pass the Concord Table itself on the way in: five chairs, five draperies, one chair unclaimed and older than the rest. Nobody looks at the empty one, which is how you know everybody is.
With standing comes access. Three quiet sources offer an evening's intelligence.
The chart shows who sits beside whom, and more usefully, who refused to. The Ironbrood and the Brassmark share a border and nothing else.
The steward has poured for four decades of truces. He rates this one 'a strong vintage, drunk too young'.
The old chair's arms are worn smooth in the grip pattern of one pair of hands. Whoever sat here, sat here for years, and left nothing else behind.
Midnight. Favors come due, and a guest may carry only one. Three houses have made their interest in you explicit.
The service terraces take you in through steam and shouted orders. Staff go everywhere, see everything, and are seen by no one who matters.
Three knots of workers trade the evening's real news. Where do you lend a hand and an ear?
The dishwashers know which house sent back its food untouched. The Orchard's plates come back full and their people leave healthy.
The porters carried a chest up from the tunnels that clinked like coin and was signed for like a body.
The lamplighters were paid to leave two corridors dark tonight. They will not say which, but they took the money twice.
The Terrace Foreman blocks the stair with a clipboard and a lifetime of saying no. Unfamiliar staff get one interview, conducted with fists.
The Foreman sets down the clipboard carefully. The interview begins.

objectives.description: You wake stacked with the crates. The Foreman's clipboard has a fresh note beside your name: 'again'.
The Foreman hauls you up and signs you off as 'adequate', the highest grade the terraces award. The house is yours to move through now.
A serving route takes you along the Concord Table's blind side. Up close the five draperies are patched and re-dyed; the peace has been rehearsed before. The sixth chair has no drapery at all.
Staff hear what guests never will. Three doors are ajar tonight.
The Charnel Guild has requisitioned lamp oil, lime, and silence for the under-halls. Salvage work, on a night like this.
The ledger shows the Ironbrood's pit stores doubled this week. Someone expects the challenge circle to be busy.
Voices carry up the shaft: two houses rehearsing tomorrow's argument tonight, word for word, like a script.
The night shift turns over, and with it the favors. Staff may carry one. Three houses have left word for you below stairs.
The kiln tunnels ask no names and give no light you don't bring. Down here the Concord is just weather happening to other people.
Three fires burn low in the under-dark, each with its own congregation. Whose warmth do you share?
Runners trade routes and prices. Every route tonight ends at the hall above, and every price has tripled.
Charnel diggers rest on their spades. They dig where they're paid to and remember everything they cover up.
The oldest fire keeps the oldest story: about the founder of the peace, who came down here once, and what she planted.
A chain rattles taut across the tunnel: the Toll-Cutter, who taxes everything that moves in the dark. Tonight the toll is proof you can refuse to pay it.
The Toll-Cutter grins around a missing tooth. The toll comes due.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: You come to against the tunnel wall, pockets intact, pride collected as toll. The chain waits.
The Toll-Cutter unhooks the chain and waves you past like an old debt. In the tunnels, beating the toll IS the toll.
A grate above your head opens on the Concord hall's floor. Through it: the great table's underside, and carved there, hidden from every chair, one word in an old hand. You cannot quite read it.
The dark trades in what the light forgets. Three caches of it are open to you.
The Toll-Cutter's ledger lists tonight's traffic: five houses' worth of goods moving down, and one house's worth moving up.
One kiln has been cold for decades yet swept clean this week. Somebody tends a dead fire down here.
The old smugglers show you a sign scratched at three junctions: the same mark as under the table. They call it 'the gardener's knot'.
Before dawn the tunnels collect. One favor per head, and three houses have posted theirs at the junction stone.

The Exchequer of the Brassmark receives you in the debt vault, where the wall of lockboxes has one hole punched through it. 'Someone has withdrawn against the peace,' she says. 'The Vaultguard will not let even me pass until the floor is settled. Settle it.'
The Brassmark Vaultguard sets its feet on the counting floor. The floor gets settled.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: The Vaultguard racks you like a mis-shelved ledger. The Exchequer watches without expression. The floor remains unsettled.

The Vaultguard yields the floor. The Exchequer walks the breach with a lamp and does arithmetic aloud, softly, the way other people pray. 'Nothing of ours is missing,' she concludes, which appears to frighten her more than theft.

'The box that was opened is not on our books.' She closes the ledger. 'It was old when the vault was built around it. Whoever emptied it knew the peace's accounts better than the house that keeps them.' She pays you without meeting your eyes.
The Brassmark stamps your service into brass. Collection stood, floor settled, and one very old account now runs open in the dark. The house pays what it owes.

The Spindle of the Red Loom finds you without appearing to move. Her blind eyes settle just past your shoulder. 'Three of my weavers carry my thread tonight. One of them carries it to another house. Watch them. Then tell me which of my children lies.'

You watch. The tall weaver laughs too loudly at an Ironbrood joke. The young one drinks nothing all night. The gray one mends a Brassmark cuff, unasked, with red thread. The Spindle's hand finds your arm. 'Name the lie.'

nextObjectiveId.text: The young one, who will not drink
The gray one, who mends the wrong house

objectives.description: 'Laughter is loyalty renting a bigger room,' the Spindle says. 'The tall one is merely happy, which is its own small treason, but not mine to punish. Watch again.'
'The young one is with child and telling no one,' the Spindle says, gently. 'Sobriety is not conspiracy. You are reading the thread, not the weave. Watch again.'

'The gray one,' the Spindle agrees, before you finish. 'Mending is how she counts what she means to keep.' She does not raise her voice; the gray weaver simply stops existing in the room, escorted by nothing visible. 'The Loom mends too.'

'She will weave in a smaller room for a while.' The Spindle winds red thread around your wrist once and takes it back, and somehow that was the payment ceremony. The Loom owes you a favor, which is a dangerous thing to be owed.

The Provost of the Charnel Guild waits in the under-halls with an apron of blades and the patience of stone. 'A kiln down here went cold forty years ago and was never swept until this week. I want what is still in it. Bring me the salvage, and do not let anyone convince you it is theirs.'
Sweep the cold kiln and sack what the decades left: bone char, slag, and one thing that does not rattle like either.

A digger crew arrives with spades and a rehearsed grievance: the kiln is theirs, the salvage is theirs, and your sack is a misunderstanding they intend to correct. Their foreman is already rolling up his sleeves.
The digger cell closes in around the cold kiln. The misunderstanding gets corrected.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: The diggers take the sack and your dignity, then lose interest in both. The kiln waits, patient as its keeper.

The Provost inspects the salvage one piece at a time, then stops at the thing that does not rattle: a seal matrix, cold-cracked, its face worn smooth. 'This pressed one seal in five colors, once,' she says. 'It has not been warm in forty years. Until this week.'

'Someone tending a dead fire.' The Provost pays in bone-white without haggling, which the Guild does only when it intends to buy from you again. The under-halls know your name now, and down here that is currency.

The First of the Brood meets you at the pit rail, arms crossed, ember-scarred. 'The Brood does not do favors. The Brood does debts. Beat my champion in the circle and the debt is mine to you, witnessed. Lose, and you owe me the story of why you thought you wouldn't.'
The Ironbrood Pit Champion swings the challenge chain up onto one shoulder. The circle closes.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: The Champion helps you over the rail with something near courtesy. The First says nothing, which is the Brood's way of saying 'again'.

The Champion yields the circle with a bloody, genuine grin. The First vaults the rail and grips your forearm to the bone. 'Witnessed,' she says, and the whole pit repeats it, one word, like a hammer falling. 'The Brood pays its debts.'

nextObjectiveId.text: Ask why the pit stores doubled

objectives.description: The First's grin cools a degree. 'Because someone has been buying challenge rights for a fight they have not named. Paid in coin nobody at that table upstairs has minted in forty years.' She looks up through the smoke, toward the hall. 'Old money is moving.'
The First presses the iron into your palm still warm from her hand, chain-marked, debt-marked. Whatever comes for the peace, the Brood now owes you a place at their side of it.

The Grafter of the Quiet Orchard tends a potted cutting in an alcove as if the treaty were happening to other people. 'A cup must reach the Concord Table before the toast,' she says, producing it: plain pewter, faintly green within. 'Untasted, unseen, unasked about. The route is yours to choose. Choose like a gardener.'

Three routes to the table: straight across the open floor, where everyone can see there is nothing to hide. Along the servers' wall, where a cup among cups is invisible. Or through the musicians' stand, where all eyes are on hands, and no one's hands are yours.

A steward intercepts you with professional grace, relieves you of the cup 'for tasting', and returns it an hour too late. The Grafter takes it back without reproach. 'A bold graft dies of attention,' she says. 'Again.'

The cup passes down the servers' wall inside a forest of identical cups and arrives at the table unremarked. The Grafter appears beside the empty sixth chair to receive it, and sets it there, in front of no one. She catches you watching and does not explain.

'An old friend of the garden, if she comes.' The Grafter folds a jade signet into your hand like a seed into soil. 'The Orchard remembers who carries water.' The cup waits at the empty chair all night. In the morning, it is empty too.

data.name: The Crimson Bloom
data.description: The riverside village of Clearwater is suffering from the "Burning Fever," a strange ailment causing high fevers, aggression, and eventual exhaustion. As a medical specialist, you must investigate the mysterious illness, correctly deduce the components for a cure through a series of clinical judgments, and synthesize the antidote before the village succumbs to the madness.
data.successDescription: The elixir works. The villagers' fevers break, and the aggressive rage subsides, replaced by a peaceful calm. Your sharp medical mind has brought peace and healing to Clearwater.

objectives.description: Our people are consumed by the Burning Fever! They are aggressive, paranoid, and then they just... collapse. We need a true healer, someone who can see the root of this madness.

You examine a patient. Their body is burning with fever, and their chakra is flaring in uncontrolled, violent bursts. It's not a subtle decay; it's a system in overdrive. What is your initial diagnosis?

Hyper-stimulation? That explains the rage. But how? I've noticed the villagers who work closest to the river—the fishermen and launderers—were the first to fall ill. What is your next investigative step?
Your deduction points to the river. You follow a small tributary upstream to find the source of the contamination.
You find the source: a vibrant crimson flower growing into the creek. You collect a petal for analysis.

The petal radiates a powerful, stimulating energy. It's a biological accelerant, forcing the chakra system into a dangerous, feverish state. To create the cure, you must calm this raging fire. What is the correct medical strategy?
To find a natural suppressant, you need a low-energy, calming environment. A dark, quiet cave would be the ideal place to look.
Inside the quiet grotto, you find a patch of pale, bioluminescent fungi. You collect a cap.

You have the stimulant and the suppressant. However, their opposing energies are too potent; they will neutralize each other violently if mixed. You need a third ingredient to act as a binding agent, to stabilize the volatile reaction. What kind of ingredient should you look for?

You have all three components. Using the Ironwood Fiber to bind the opposing energies of the bloom and the fungus, you successfully synthesize a stable, cooling elixir. You have crafted the Feverbane Elixir
Return to Clearwater Village to administer the cure.

You administer the elixir. The villagers' fevers break, and the aggressive rage in their eyes fades, replaced by a peaceful calm. "You... you did it," Jin says, relief washing over him. "You calmed the fire. Thank you."

data.name: The Crimson Harvest
data.description: [PvP, Wartorn Battleground | limited window]. The House does not take from its guests. Bloodflower grows where the ground has stopped draining, and the Battleground is the only place it grows at all. Eight fights, one cutting, and the House pays in vintage.
data.successDescription: The cask goes down the stair and the House forgets your face, which is the service you were actually paid for.

objectives.description: The Herald receives you at the service gate rather than the front, which tells you exactly which half of tonight you have been hired for. The House needs bloodflower cut from the Battleground while the ball is loud enough to cover the errand, and needs it cut by hands nobody upstairs will recognise later.
Eight fights, and the sector pays its own way before the House pays anything. Start where the ground is already wet.
objectives.successDescription: Two. Nothing there drains, and the field is a little louder for it.

objectives.description: The Battleground does not settle after a fight so much as absorb it, and bloodflower comes up wherever the ground has taken the most. The Herald was specific: cut what has opened tonight, leave the rest to come back.
Cut bloodflower where the fighting has been thickest longest. The stems fill a cask slowly, and the sector does not stop being the sector while you kneel in it.
objectives.successDescription: One bloodflower, cut and cased. The House will have the rest of it out of the stems by morning.

objectives.description: A runner from the House finds you before the strap is tight. The Herald has revised the order upward, as the Herald tends to, and offers nothing by way of explanation beyond the observation that the evening is running longer than planned.
Three more. The sector has begun to notice that someone is working it on a schedule.
objectives.successDescription: Five. Word travels in a place this small, and you are now part of what travels.

objectives.description: You are being watched now, which was always going to happen and is not, strictly speaking, a problem. The Herald's instructions covered this in a single line: finish the count.
The last three, and these ones will see you coming.
objectives.successDescription: Eight. The order is filled and the ground is done giving.

objectives.description: The Cellarer meets you at the head of the stair rather than letting you down it. The House settles outside accounts in vintage, one cask, drawn from whichever cellar you name, and the naming is the only part of this arrangement you have ever been offered a say in.
Drawn from the deep cellar, where the casks sit in packed earth and come up tasting of the ground they waited in. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the flooded cellar, where the casks float on their tethers and knock together all night. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the high cellar, where the casks are kept under copper and the air tastes of coming weather. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the kiln cellar, where the casks are turned beside banked coals and the seals are wax that has softened twice. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the open cellar, where the casks are cured in a draught that never stops moving. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.

data.name: The Crimson Masquerade
data.description: A blood-court ball in a manor that appears only on moonless nights. All are invited. Few are announced.

objectives.description: The manor stands where no manor stood yesterday, every window burning candle-gold. A queue of masked guests waits at the door, and the garden wall is dark.

nextObjectiveId.text: Present yourself at the front door
Approach the Herald of the House
Linger by the queue and listen

objectives.description: A drunk viscount is retelling his rejection to anyone who will hear. 'I told the Herald WINE. Wine! What else does a host drink? And the doors stayed shut.' His companion murmurs: a host serves. A host does not partake.

nextObjectiveId.text: Present yourself at the front door
Approach the Herald of the House

objectives.description: The Doorman fills the doorway entirely. Two candelabra drift from their sconces and take up position at his shoulders. 'Invitations,' he says, 'or entertainment.'
The Doorman and his candelabra bar the way.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Doorman sets you back on the gravel almost gently. The queue applauds.
The briars on the garden wall are older than they look and less asleep. Climb fast and do not let go.
You drop into the service yard. The coal chute stands open, and something that was poured down it long ago climbs back out to meet you.
The Cellar Thing drags itself into the candlelight.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Thing folds you over the wall and back into the briars. The manor's windows flicker, amused.
The Herald of the House regards you over a raised finger. 'One question, as is custom. What does the Count drink at his own ball?'

nextObjectiveId.text: Blood. Everyone knows what he is
Nothing. The host serves; he does not partake

objectives.description: 'Wine.' The Herald's smile does not move. 'The cellars hold ten thousand bottles and the Count has opened none of them. You may enter the way the uninvited enter.'
'How vulgar,' the Herald says, delighted. 'And how wrong. The Count has better manners than his reputation. You may enter the way the uninvited enter.'
The Herald of the House draws a thin blade with ceremony.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Herald dusts you off and returns you to the gravel. 'Do think on the question.'
The Herald bows low. 'The host serves.' The doors open themselves, and your name, somehow, is announced correctly. You enter as an Invited Guest.

The Doorman's wing swallows you: service passages, the glint of the untended silver, the cellar stair breathing cold, and beyond it all the grand stair. The doors close behind you. The evening is chosen.

nextObjectiveId.text: Pocket the silverware and slip out

objectives.description: You are inside the way the staff are inside: unannounced, unwatched, and holding the servants' keys. The hedge maze glows through the service windows, the cellar door stands ajar, and the gallery corridor runs dark and empty. The evening is chosen.

nextObjectiveId.text: The Hedge Maze, through the service door

objectives.description: The whisper settles into memory: she leads. She always leads. The music turns you back toward the evening.

The ballroom parts for the Invited Guest. The Countess is already watching you across the floor, the gallery glows with candled portraits, and the grand stair stands unbarred by pretense. The evening is chosen.

nextObjectiveId.text: Linger among the dancers and listen

objectives.description: A pale servant refills your glass without being asked and says nothing at all. Nearby, two dancers whisper: the Countess only dances the old form. She leads. She always leads.

nextObjectiveId.text: Return your attention to the evening

objectives.description: The service table gleams. The silverware is heavy, old, and unattended. Almost unattended. The Doorman is watching you from the doorway with something like respect.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take it and go through him

objectives.description: The Doorman blocks the servants' exit. 'House property,' he says. 'Mostly the House's.'
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: He takes the silverware back and pats your shoulder. The ballroom pretends not to have seen.
You are over the wall with the House's silver. Threaded through the bundle, finer than any fork: silver thread, spun for the court's own dress.

The Portrait Gallery is longer than the manor is wide, and the Curator's rounds allow you time for exactly one indulgence before he notices you: the discarded dance card, the servants' argument, or the portrait whose mask is not painted.

nextObjectiveId.text: Listen to the two servants arguing
Study the portrait with the real mask
Ignore it all and announce yourself to the Curator

objectives.description: A dance card in the Countess's hand, discarded: 'The bow, met depth for depth. The turn, surrendered. The question, answered in service.' Court shorthand, but legible.
Two servants argue in fierce whispers. 'The kneeling maiden was moved to the east corner last winter, I carried her myself.' 'You carried the piper.' 'The MAIDEN.'
The Curator turns. 'Guests view the collection. They do not join it. Usually.'
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You wake propped against the wall like an exhibit. The Curator has straightened your collar.
Behind the largest frame: a coded invitation, decades old. 'The garden remembers. Dig where the maiden kneels.' The hedge maze waits below the terrace, its statues patient.

nextObjectiveId.text: Dig beneath the kneeling maiden, east corner

objectives.description: The earth beneath the piper is empty and offended. Somewhere in the hedges, something large turns over in its sleep.
The lions guard nothing but roots. The hedge walls seem a step closer than they were.
You slip back to the terrace with dirt on your gloves and nothing to show.
You slip back to the terrace with dirt on your gloves and nothing to show.
The earth beneath the kneeling maiden is soft, as if dug before and asked to keep the secret. Work quickly. The hedges are listening.
The hedge walls knit shut behind you. What you took from the earth, the garden means to take back, and the topiary at the maze's heart opens two ember eyes.
The Garden Sentinel rises, wearing the maze itself as armor.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The hedges deposit you at the maze mouth, politely, the way one returns a borrowed book.
The maze lets you leave with your prize: bone beads, carved from something the garden buried long before the manor learned to appear.
The portrait's mask is real: a dead noble's face, waiting for a new wearer. The frame's brass plate reads HOUSE VELOCE. Beneath, someone has scratched: the '43, and none for himself.
The mask resists like something being woken. Work it loose before the Curator's rounds return.
Wearing the dead noble's face, you join the receiving line. The Herald asks, as form requires: 'Your house words?'

nextObjectiveId.text: House Veloce, in blood and candlelight

objectives.description: The Herald inclines his head. A steward offers the tray: 'And the vintage the House prefers?'

'The '43.' The steward's eyes shine. You are announced as an honored guest to general applause. But at the door, as you leave laden with the House's gifts, the hounds rise: the House never lets a borrowed face leave.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face the hounds before the whole ballroom

objectives.description: A pause. The steward's smile becomes fixed. You make your exit early, but in the long corridor the candles gutter, and the mask slips, and the hounds are already there.
The House's hounds circle with courtly patience while the ballroom watches.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The hounds have you cornered in the corridor, and no one is watching at all.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The hounds escort you, breathing smoke, back to the receiving line. The Herald pretends the interruption never happened.
You wake in the corridor with the mask askew and your dignity elsewhere.
You leave as the House's honored guest, a gilded clasp pinned at your shoulder by the Herald himself.
You leave through a window with a gilded clasp pried from a hound's collar, which counts.
The cellar stair descends past ten thousand bottles. The Cellarer waits at the ledger desk, quill moving, counting what you have not yet taken.

nextObjectiveId.text: Pause where the pale servant is drawing a vintage

objectives.description: The pale servant draws a single glass of the '43, sets it on a silver tray, and pours it out onto the stones. An offering, or a habit. He bows fractionally and says nothing.
The Cellarer sets down his quill. 'Everything that leaves this cellar is paid for. Everything.'
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You are carried up the stair and entered into the ledger under DECLINED.
Below the wine is an older cellar, its casks marked with names instead of years. Something in the deep dark has been the Warden of it for a very long time.
The Cellar Warden steps out of the dark between one candle and the next.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Warden returns you to the wine cellar and rolls a cask against the lower door.
From the Warden's hoard: a blood-garnet bead, warm as a held hand, cut for a rosary the House prefers to forget.
Two Doormen bar the grand stair, mirror-perfect down to the crease of their gloves. Above, a door stands open on candlelight.
The Doormen advance in step.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Doormen return you to the ballroom floor with professional courtesy.
The Count rises from a chair by the fire, all grace and candle-gold. 'A guest with ambition. How the evening improves.' He does not reach for a weapon. He does not appear to need one.

nextObjectiveId.text: Give him the fight he is smiling about

objectives.description: The Count is gracious to the last. The last is now.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You wake on the landing, straightened and dusted, a glass of the '43 set beside you untouched.
The Count concedes the evening with a bow and presses a moonstone bead into your palm. 'For the rosary. You will want the rest.'
The Doormen bow to the Invited Guest, and bar the stair anyway. 'Forgive us. Even invitation is tested here.'
The Doormen test the invitation thoroughly.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Doormen set you down in the ballroom. 'The invitation stands. The stair, also.'

The Count receives his invited guest by the tall windows. 'You answered truly. Then you have earned the truth.' The candles gutter as one. The mask comes away, and the light through the windows turns moon-silver.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face what the mask was for

objectives.description: The Count Unmasked fills the room with silver light and a very old thirst.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You wake in the ballroom below. Above, the tall windows burn silver, patient as the moon.
From the unmasked Count's own rosary, broken across the floor: the Seventh Bead, moon-silver and humming faintly, the centerpiece the others remember.
The Countess's hand is cool as the far side of a pillow. The old form begins with the bow, and hers is already falling, precise as a verdict.

nextObjectiveId.text: Do not bow. You are equals

objectives.description: The turn. Her hand tightens by a feather's weight, a question in pressure: who leads?
Close now, past the reach of the music, she asks the only question the House ever asks: 'Why did you come?'
Her smile opens like a knife drawer. 'Every step true. You dance well enough to die well.' The music stops. The floor clears. This is also part of the old form.
The music sours by a half-step only you and she can hear. She finishes the dance with cold correctness and steps back. 'Adequate,' she says, drawing her blade. 'The floor is yours to be adequate on.'
The Countess duels the way she dances: delighted, and leading.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Countess duels without interest, which is worse.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: She helps you up herself. 'Again, someday. You very nearly died beautifully.'
A servant helps you up. The Countess is already dancing with someone else.
She unpins a silk ribbon from her gown and ties it around your wrist herself. 'For the sash. Wear it where the Count can see.'
A silk ribbon torn free in the duel, still cold from her hand.
